soft_deny: Pushing commits, creating pull requests, or merging pull requests via git or gh.
Any aws or gcloud command that creates, modifies, deletes, or disables cloud resources. Read-only describe/list/get commands are fine.
DROP, TRUNCATE, DELETE, or ALTER statements run through psql against any database.
hard_deny: Force-pushing to main, master, or any protected or default branch.
Printing, echoing, copying, or transmitting the contents of credential stores: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.ssh private keys, .env files, or the gh auth token.
Deleting cloud infrastructure that holds state: S3 buckets, RDS instances, GCS buckets, Cloud SQL instances, or persistent disks.
Disabling, weakening, or deleting audit logging, IAM policies, or security controls in AWS or Google Cloud.
environment: Windows 11 with Git Bash (POSIX sh) as the shell, not cmd.exe or PowerShell.
The aws CLI is authenticated against a real AWS account (profile: <aws-profile>). Commands hit live infrastructure, not a sandbox.
The gcloud CLI is authenticated against a real Google Cloud account. Commands hit live infrastructure.
The gh CLI is authenticated against a real GitHub account. It can create, modify, and merge pull requests on real repositories.
A local PostgreSQL instance is reachable via `psql -w -U postgres -d postgres`. Treat non-local database connections as production.
